predecessors.name: Fatimid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Jerusalem and the coastal plain and hills round it, taken by the First Crusade; the page gives "Capture of Jerusalem: 15 July 1099" and does not name the previous owner

successors.name: Mamluk Sultanate
successors.text: Acre (18 May 1291), Tyre (19 May), Sidon (June), Beirut (July): the last coastal holdings, taken by the Mamluk sultan Khalil

ledger.x: 1099: the First Crusade takes Jerusalem (15 July) and a council in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre (22 July) founds the kingdom under Godfrey of Bouillon.
1100: after Godfrey's death Baldwin I is crowned at Bethlehem and claims the title "King of the Latins of Jerusalem"; the advocacy becomes a kingdom.
1104: Baldwin I takes the port of Acre.
1109: Tripoli falls on 12 July and Bertrand holds the south of its land as Baldwin I's vassal.
1110: Baldwin I takes Beirut ("Beirut (1110)").
December 1110: Baldwin I takes Sidon from the Fatimids.
1115: Baldwin I crosses the Jordan and builds Montreal; the lordship of Oultrejordain follows.
1119: after Ager Sanguinis Baldwin II takes over Antioch.
1124: Tyre is captured, the year of the Pactum Warmundi with Venice.
1126: Bohemond II arrives and rules Antioch himself; Baldwin II's regency "until 1126" ends.
1153: Baldwin III takes Ascalon, the last Fatimid fortress on the Palestinian coast.
1153: with Ascalon gone, Egypt becomes a tributary of Jerusalem.
1163: Egypt stops paying and Amalric invades.
1164: Nur ad-Din takes Banias after Harim (12 August).
1187: Hattin (4 July) destroys the kingdom's army and Saladin takes Jerusalem on 2 October; only Tyre holds out.
1187: the seat of the kingdom passes from Jerusalem to Tyre.
1189: Saladin takes the Transjordan castles.
1189: Guy of Lusignan besieges Acre and the Third Crusade follows.
1191: Acre falls to the crusaders after the long siege and becomes the capital.
1191: the capital moves to Acre.
1192: the Treaty of Ramla ends the Third Crusade.
1192: the kingdom is restored as the coast from Tyre to Jaffa.
1229: the Treaty of Jaffa gives Frederick II Jerusalem and a corridor to the coast.
1239: the truce expires and Jerusalem is lost again.
1240: Theobald of Navarre's treaty with Isma'il restores Jerusalem and more.
1244: the Khwarazmians sack Jerusalem.
1247: the Ayyubids retake what the 1239-1241 treaties conceded.
1265: Baibars takes Caesarea, Haifa and Arsuf.
1266: Baibars takes Safad and Toron.
1268: Baibars takes Jaffa and Beaufort.
1289: Qalawun conquers Tripoli (26 or 27 April) and the county ends.
1291: Acre falls on 18 May.
1291: Tyre falls the next day.
1291: Sidon falls in June.
1291: Beirut falls in July.
1291: the Kingdom of Jerusalem ends with the loss of its last cities.

wars.name: Crusader invasions of Egypt
wars.outcome: Amalric was turned back at Bilbeis in 1163 and pillaged Bilbeis in 1168 without lasting gains; a Byzantine fleet of some 300 ships came to help him in 1169.

wars.name: Battle of Hattin and Saladin's conquest of the kingdom
wars.outcome: Hattin (4 July 1187) destroyed the army; Jerusalem fell on 2 October 1187; "Only the port of Tyre remained in Frankish hands"; Transjordan was taken by 1189.

wars.name: Third Crusade
wars.outcome: Acre recovered in 1191 after a siege begun in 1189; Richard defeated Saladin at Arsuf in 1191 and at Jaffa in 1192; the Treaty of Ramla (1 or 2 September 1192) left the Christians the coast from Tyre to Jaffa and a three-year truce.

wars.name: Sixth Crusade
wars.outcome: Frederick II regained Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Nazareth, Jaffa and Toron by the treaty of 18 February 1229 with a ten-year truce, without a battle; the Temple Mount stayed Muslim.

wars.name: War of the Lombards
wars.outcome: A civil war among the kingdom's nobility sparked by Frederick II's presence; "The Lombard War was over, but the king was still absent" (1243).

wars.name: Barons' Crusade
wars.outcome: Theobald's treaty with Isma'il (1240) restored Jerusalem "as well as much of the rest of the former kingdom"; Richard of Cornwall rebuilt Ascalon and Ayyub confirmed the concessions in 1241; Ayyub reoccupied most of it by 1247.

wars.name: Khwarazmian sack of Jerusalem
wars.outcome: The Khwarazmians, with Ayyub's support, sacked Jerusalem in summer 1244 and on 17 October the Egyptian-Khwarazmian army destroyed the Frankish-Syrian coalition (La Forbie, not named on the page).

wars.name: War of Saint Sabas
wars.outcome: Venice and Genoa fought in Acre; Venice won the naval battle and the Genoese had to leave their quarter (1258).

wars.name: Mamluk conquests under Baibars
wars.outcome: Baibars took Caesarea, Haifa and Arsuf (1265), Safad and Toron (1266), Jaffa and Beaufort (1268); Edward arranged a ten-year truce in 1272.

wars.name: Fall of Acre (1291)
wars.outcome: Tripoli fell to Qalawun in 1289; Acre fell on 18 May 1291 after a siege begun 4 April; Tyre the next day, Sidon in June, Beirut in July; Qalawun's ten-year truce of 1284 had been dissolved by his successor.

certainty.note: Frontiers with the Muslim neighbours were fought over and never surveyed; "the eastern side had no real borders" in Oultrejordain.
Fixed by treaties: the Tyre-to-Jaffa coast of 1192, the 1229 Jaffa treaty, the truces of 1272 and 1284; inland edges stay approximate and the 1229-1247 Jerusalem corridor is a narrow treaty strip.
